module_title: Choosing and Setting Up Your Sales Location

lessons.title: Choosing Between Market Stall, Shop, or Online Selling
lessons.body: When starting your okrika business, you must decide where to sell. The three main options are a market stall, a shop, or online selling. Each has pros and cons. A market stall is the most common starting point. In places like Lagos, Nairobi, or Accra, you can rent a small stall in a busy market for between 5,000 and 20,000 naira per month (or equivalent). The advantage is high foot trafficâpeople already come to the market to buy. But competition is fierce, and you must be present daily. A shop gives you more control. You can lock up your goods, set your own hours, and create a brand. But rent is higherâmaybe 50,000 to 200,000 naira monthly in a good area. You also need to attract customers, not just rely on passersby. Online selling is growing fast. You can use WhatsApp, Facebook Marketplace, Jumia, or Instagram to reach customers beyond your neighborhood. You avoid rent, but you must pay for data, take good photos, and arrange delivery. Trust is harder to build online. Many successful okrika sellers start with a market stall, then move to a shop as they grow, and add online selling to reach more people. Consider your capital, your tolerance for risk, and your target customers. If you have little money, start with a stall or online. If you have savings, a shop might be better. Test your market before committing to a long lease. Talk to other traders about what works. Remember, location is not permanentâyou can change as your business grows.

lessons.title: Negotiating Rent and Understanding Market Fees
lessons.body: Rent and fees can eat your profit if you don't negotiate well. In most African markets, rent is negotiable. Never accept the first price. For a market stall, start by asking other traders what they pay. Then offer 20-30% less than the asking price. Be polite but firm. If the landlord refuses, walk awayâthere is always another space. For a shop, ask for a monthly rate, but also ask about quarterly or yearly discounts. Many landlords prefer long-term tenants and will reduce rent if you pay upfront. For example, if monthly rent is 100,000 naira, you might negotiate 900,000 for a year (a 25% saving). Besides rent, there are market fees. These include daily tolls (often 200-500 naira), security fees, and cleaning fees. Some markets charge a 'ticket' for each sale. Always ask for a breakdown before you sign anything. Get a written agreement, even if it's just a handwritten note signed by both parties. Include the rent amount, payment dates, and what is covered. If you sell online, you may pay commission to platforms like Jumia (usually 5-15% per sale). For WhatsApp selling, there are no fees, but you pay for data and delivery. Budget for these costs. A good rule: total location costs should not exceed 20% of your expected monthly sales. If rent is too high, consider sharing a stall with another trader or starting online. Also, be aware of hidden costs like electricity, water, or 'goodwill' payments to local officials. Ask questions. Talk to fellow traders. Negotiation is a skillâpractice it.

lessons.title: Setting Up a Attractive Stall Layout
lessons.body: An attractive stall layout can increase your sales by 30% or more. The key is to make it easy for customers to see and touch your clothes. Start with a clean, well-lit space. If you have a stall, use a tarpaulin or umbrella for shade. Arrange clothes by category: men's shirts, women's dresses, children's wear, etc. Use a simple rail or rope to hang itemsânever pile them in a heap. Hang the most colorful or unique pieces at eye level. Use a table for folded items like jeans or t-shirts. Place a mirror so customers can see how they look. Price tags are essential. Write prices clearly with a marker on cardboard or use stickers. In many African markets, customers expect to bargain, so set prices 10-20% higher than your minimum. Create a focal pointâa mannequin or a display of your best outfitâto draw people in. Keep the stall tidy. Re-fold clothes after customers touch them. Use baskets or boxes for accessories like belts, scarves, and bags. If you have a shop, use the walls for shelving. Paint the walls a bright color like yellow or blue to stand out. Add a small chair for customers to sit while trying on shoes. For online selling, take photos against a plain background. Use natural light. Show the clothes on a person or mannequin. Group similar items in one photo. Your layout should tell a story: 'Come in, find a treasure.' Change your display weekly to keep it fresh. A good layout invites customers to linger and buy more.

lessons.title: Security and Theft Prevention for Your Stock
lessons.body: Thrift shops are targets for thieves because the goods are valuable and easy to resell. You must protect your stock. First, secure your stall or shop. If you have a shop, install a strong door with a good padlock. For a stall, use a lockable metal box or cage. Never leave goods overnight in an open stall. If you must, pack them in sacks and take them home. Second, control access. In a busy market, customers brush against each other. Hire a trusted assistant to watch the crowd. Keep your cash in a money belt or a locked drawerânever in an open box. Third, mark your items. Use a permanent marker to write your initials or a small symbol on the inside label. This makes it harder for thieves to resell and easier for you to identify stolen goods. Fourth, build relationships with neighbors. Other traders can watch your stall when you step away. Join or form a traders' security group where you contribute a small amount weekly for a night guard. Fifth, be alert to common tricks. Some thieves work in pairs: one distracts you while the other steals. Others pretend to bargain loudly while slipping items into bags. Train your staff to greet every customer and offer helpâthis discourages theft. Keep a record of your inventory. Count your stock at the start and end of each day. If you sell online, use a delivery service with tracking. For high-value items, consider a small safe. Insurance is rare in informal markets, so prevention is your best policy. A few simple steps can save you thousands.

lessons.title: Creating a Welcoming Atmosphere for Customers
lessons.body: Customers buy more when they feel welcome. A welcoming atmosphere starts with you. Greet every person who comes near your stall with a smile and a friendly 'Welcome, come and see.' In many African cultures, greetings are importantâask about their day or family. Don't hover or pressure them. Let them browse. Play soft music if you canâa small radio or phone speaker works. Keep your stall clean and organized. A dirty, cluttered space drives people away. Offer a chair or stool for elderly customers or those trying on shoes. If you have a shop, provide a small mirror and a curtained area for trying on clothes. This makes customers feel comfortable and more likely to buy. Use local languages to connect. If you speak the customer's language, use it. Offer a small discount for repeat customers or a free gift (like a scarf) with a large purchase. Be patient with bargainingâit's part of the culture. Never argue. If a price is too low, politely say no and offer a counter. Thank every customer, even if they don't buy. They may return. Keep your promises: if you say you'll hold an item, do it. Trust builds loyalty. In online selling, respond quickly to messages. Use a friendly tone. Send a thank-you message after each sale. Ask for feedback. A welcoming atmosphere turns one-time buyers into regulars. It also encourages word-of-mouth, which is free advertising. Remember, people buy from people they like. Your attitude is as important as your clothes.

lessons.title: Managing Space for Storage and Display
lessons.body: Space is money in a thrift business. You need to store stock and display it without crowding. Start by sorting your clothes into three groups: display (best items), backstock (extra sizes or colors), and repair (items needing fixing). For a market stall, use vertical space. Hang a rope or wire across the top of your stall and use hangers to display clothes at different heights. Use stackable plastic crates or cardboard boxes for backstock. Label each box clearly (e.g., 'Men's Shirts M-L'). Keep them under your table or behind your stall. For a shop, install shelves on walls. Use the highest shelves for backstock and lower shelves for display. A rolling rack can double as a display and storage. For online selling, store items in clear plastic bags with labels. Keep a digital inventory on your phone using a simple app like Google Sheets or a notebook. Rotate your stock. Move older items to the front and bring new items to the back. This keeps your display fresh and helps you track what sells. Don't overstock. Too many clothes make it hard for customers to find what they want. Aim to display only 20-30 items at a time. If you have a lot of stock, consider a small storage unit or a locked trunk at home. For traveling vendors, use a large suitcase with wheels. Pack items tightly to save space. Always keep a 'grab bag' of small accessories near the front for impulse buys. Review your space monthly. If an item hasn't sold in 3 months, move it to a discount bin. Efficient space management means more sales and less waste.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of a market stall over a shop?
options: A) Lower rent and high foot traffic
C) Ability to lock up goods
quiz.explanation: Market stalls are cheaper and benefit from existing customer flow.

quiz.q: When negotiating rent for a market stall, what should you do first?
options: B) Ask other traders what they pay
quiz.explanation: Knowing the typical rate gives you bargaining power.

quiz.q: Which of these is a hidden cost in a market?
options: B) Daily tolls and security fees
quiz.explanation: Daily tolls and security fees are common extra charges in African markets.

quiz.q: What percentage of expected monthly sales should location costs ideally not exceed?
quiz.explanation: Keeping location costs under 20% helps ensure profitability.

quiz.q: Why is a written agreement important when renting a stall?
options: B) It prevents misunderstandings about rent and fees
C) It is required by law
D) It allows you to skip payments
quiz.explanation: A written record clarifies terms and protects both parties.

quiz.q: What is a good strategy for displaying clothes in a stall?
options: A) Pile them in a heap
B) Hang them at eye level
quiz.explanation: Hanging at eye level makes items visible and easy to browse.

quiz.q: Why should you use price tags?
options: B) To save time and reduce confusion
quiz.explanation: Price tags reduce repetitive questions and help customers decide.

quiz.q: What is a focal point in a stall layout?
options: A) A mannequin or display of best outfit
quiz.explanation: A focal point draws customers' attention and invites them in.

quiz.q: How often should you change your display?
options: D) Only when items sell out
quiz.explanation: Changing weekly keeps the stall fresh and encourages repeat visits.

quiz.q: For online selling, what background is best for photos?
quiz.explanation: A plain background makes the clothes stand out.

quiz.q: What is a common theft trick in thrift shops?
options: B) Two thieves working together to distract
quiz.explanation: Distraction is a common method used by thieves in pairs.

quiz.q: How can you mark your items to deter theft?
options: A) Write your initials on the label
D) Keep them in the open
quiz.explanation: Marking items makes them harder to resell and easier to identify.

quiz.q: What should you do with cash during busy market hours?
options: A) Keep it in an open box
B) Use a money belt or locked drawer
D) Give it to a neighbor
quiz.explanation: Securing cash prevents easy theft.

quiz.q: Why is it important to build relationships with neighboring traders?
options: A) They can watch your stall when you step away
B) They will give you free goods
C) They will pay your rent
D) They will advertise for you
quiz.explanation: Neighbors can provide informal security and support.

quiz.q: What is a good way to prevent theft when selling online?
options: A) Use a delivery service with tracking
quiz.explanation: Tracking ensures delivery and reduces fraud.

quiz.q: Why should you greet every customer?
options: A) It is required by law
B) It makes them feel welcome and more likely to buy
quiz.explanation: A friendly greeting creates a positive shopping experience.

quiz.q: What is a simple way to make your stall more welcoming?
quiz.explanation: Soft music can relax customers and encourage browsing.

quiz.q: Why should you offer a chair to elderly customers?
options: A) To make them comfortable and stay longer
quiz.explanation: Comfort increases the chance of a sale.

quiz.q: What should you do if a customer bargains too low?
options: B) Politely say no and offer a counter
quiz.explanation: Politely countering maintains respect and profit.

quiz.q: Why is it important to thank customers even if they don't buy?
options: B) It is a waste of time
quiz.explanation: A good impression encourages repeat visits.

quiz.q: What is a good way to organize backstock in a stall?
options: A) Use stackable crates with labels
quiz.explanation: Crates with labels keep stock organized and accessible.

quiz.q: Why should you rotate your stock?
options: A) To keep display fresh and track sales
quiz.explanation: Rotation helps you identify what sells and keeps the stall attractive.

quiz.q: How many items should you display at a time?
quiz.explanation: Displaying 20-30 items avoids clutter and makes browsing easier.

quiz.q: What should you do with items that haven't sold in 3 months?
quiz.explanation: Discounting clears slow-moving stock and frees space.

quiz.q: For online selling, how can you keep track of inventory?
options: A) Use a notebook or Google Sheets
quiz.explanation: A simple digital or paper record helps manage stock.

quiz.q: What is a 'grab bag' in a thrift stall?
options: A) A bag of small accessories for impulse buys
D) A bag for rent money
quiz.explanation: Accessories near the front encourage quick purchases.

quiz.q: Why is vertical space important in a stall?
options: A) It allows more display without crowding
quiz.explanation: Using height maximizes limited space.

quiz.q: What should you do before signing a lease for a shop?
options: A) Ask for a breakdown of all fees
C) Pay in cash without receipt
quiz.explanation: Knowing all costs prevents surprises.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of selling online?
quiz.explanation: Online selling avoids physical location costs.

quiz.q: What is a common market fee?
quiz.explanation: Daily tolls are common in African markets.
